findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_friction.py:1095 calls process_label() inside route_event, whose handler at line 1105 is `except RuntimeError`. The new process_label (diff lines ~430-448) propagates read_platform_config errors unchanged, and tests/test_friction_strict_log.py:89 asserts a ValueError('bad toml') propagates. design.md decision 1 says configuration errors become pending routes, but this holds only for RuntimeError. One bad value therefore aborts the whole route_pending loop, which design.md rejected for the destination case. The same applies to non-RuntimeError failures from read_operator_config in destination_for. Not verified: which exception types read_operator_config raises.
findings.summary: A label configuration error that is not a RuntimeError (e.g. a ValueError from a TOML parse failure, which the new code deliberately propagates) escapes route_event as an exception. It does not become a retained `pending` route, so it can abort route_pending and the callers that route after a record has been written.
